subject: Banking
title: Monthly Maintenance Fees
description: A quick, practical guide to Monthly Maintenance Fees.

hook.text: Some banks charge $12-15 per month just to keep your account open. That's $180 per year for the privilege of a balance.

buildup.text: Maintenance fees are waived if you maintain a minimum balance, usually $1,500-$5,000. Poorer customers can't qualify.

discovery.text: Banks profit twice: earn interest on the required minimum balance and collect fees from anyone who can't maintain it.

twist.text: Online banks eliminated maintenance fees. The fee survives only because traditional banks have branches to fund.

climax.text: Maintenance fees punish small balances. The less money you have, the more banking costs you.

punchline.text: $180 per year to hold your money. Minimum balance rules favor the wealthy.

quiz.question: How can maintenance fees typically be avoided?

details.summary: Monthly maintenance fees on checking and savings accounts generate billions for banks, typically charging $5 to $25 per month for the privilege of holding your money. These fees disproportionately affect low-balance customers who cannot meet waiver thresholds.
details.whyItMatters: Monthly fees create a poverty tax where the least wealthy customers pay the most for basic banking. Understanding these fees reveals why financial inclusion advocates push for free basic banking services.
takeaways: Average checking account maintenance fees range from $5 to $25 monthly
Fees are typically waived for customers maintaining minimum balances of $1,000-$5,000
Low-income customers disproportionately pay maintenance fees

faq.question: Why do banks charge monthly maintenance fees?
faq.answer: Banks argue that small accounts cost more to maintain than they generate in interest income. Monthly fees ensure these accounts are profitable. In practice, fees often exceed the actual cost of servicing, making them a significant profit center.

faq.question: How can you avoid monthly maintenance fees?
faq.answer: Maintain minimum balance requirements, set up direct deposit, use online-only accounts from neobanks that charge no fees, or switch to a credit union. Many banks waive fees for customers who meet specific activity or balance thresholds.
